post.caption: Rolex's Oyster survived an unfinished swim. In 1926 Rolex introduced the Oyster, its first waterproof wristwatch. In 1927 Mercedes Gleitze swam the English Channel, the first British woman to do it. Doubts followed, so she agreed to a second swim in colder water, and Rolex founder Hans Wilsdorf gave her an Oyster to wear. She became Rolex's first sporting ambassador. On 21 October 1927 she gave up that swim after 10 hours and 24 minutes. The watch still came out in perfect working order, and Rolex ran an advert in the Daily Mail.
